findings.disposition_reason: The near-coincidence is the measurement: the two weighted spectra agree to a few thousandths of unity between eigenvalue fractions 0.13 and 0.95, so the grey line has no separate path to show there, and the difference the panel exists to report is visible at both ends, where collocation leaves the drawn 0 and 1 rules at about -0.12 and 1.12 while Galerkin stays inside them.
findings.summary: In the left panel the dashed collocation series is drawn beneath the Galerkin series, and because the two weighted spectra nearly coincide, grey pixels cover only 16-30 per 40-pixel column strip against 140-250 for the purple line between eigenvalue fractions 0.13 and 0.95: a reader sees the collocation curve only as short dash ends either side of zero and above one, and cannot follow it across the middle of the panel.

findings.disposition_reason: The rules are 1.2 pt dotted against the series' 2.6 pt dashed, and the caption states that dotted grey lines mark 0 and 1, so the two roles are separated by weight and by the caption rather than by hue.
findings.summary: The 0 and 1 bound rules are dotted in the same grey (#929292) as the collocation series, so a reader must use the caption to tell which grey marks are the bounds and which are measured data; the right panel carries no equivalent grey reference at all, so the grey dash there reads unambiguously as data.
